Two design gaps were found and fixed while building the retry path: (1) compileGap deduplicated ANY existing run, so a job retry with the same idempotency key could never re-run the pipeline and a crashed in-flight run would be 'completed' prematurely — added resumeExisting semantics (re-enter the run, reuse recorded steps, skip stages already reached) and attempt-scoped keys (user key for attempt 1, K#attempt-N after); (2) curricula now carry run_id (migration 003) so a resumed run re-enters its own curriculum instead of creating a second course, and artefact ids are deterministic (lesson:kind:segment:version) with addArtefact idempotent on them, so no audio is duplicated across a restart.

GAP-019.notes: Found by reading a GREEN CI run's Postgres server log. Migration 001 declared UNIQUE (lesson_id, kind, version) on artefacts, encoding the assumption that a lesson has one artefact per kind. True for a transcript, false for audio: a script is synthesised as several segments, all kind='audio' at version 1, so the second insert violated the constraint. The insert threw, the pipeline's audio fallback caught it and degraded the lesson to transcript-only, and the run still reported success — an audio-first product shipping without audio, with only a warning line. The in-memory store has no constraints, so the memory journey passed throughout. Fixed by forward-only migration 002 adding segment_ordinal and a segment-aware unique constraint; the shared contract suite now stores four audio segments for one lesson so memory and SQL are held to the same behaviour, and both journeys assert audio publishes rather than only that the compile succeeded.

GAP-013.notes: The capability library is now wired into compilation. classifyPriorCapabilities (domain) splits prior filled gaps' objectives + target capability into satisfied (>= 0.6 reuse threshold) and decayed. compile.ts recalls prior capabilities (stage B), passes satisfied into the planner's satisfiedExternalPrerequisites AND the learner brief (so the planner can copy them verbatim), and hands decayed capabilities to the diagnostic as material to re-demonstrate. Step input versions include the new inputs so retries stay idempotent. Search was already done; edges were already written on fill — the read side was missing.

GAP-018.notes: Vector retrieval replaces lexical-only chunk search. Migration 004 adds a pgvector embedding column (vector(384), HNSW index); searchChunks takes an optional query embedding and ranks by cosine (pgvector <=> on SQL, cosineSimilarity on memory), falling back to full-text/term retrieval when the deployment has no embedding capability. New guarded Embeddings adapter in provider-adapters (budget check before the call, usage recorded, undefined = no capability), a scripted deterministic fake, and a live OpenAI-compatible backend. The pipeline embeds each source's chunks (embed_chunk step) and the query (embed_query step, keyed so a resumed run reuses the vector instead of re-charging) and passes the vector to retrieval. The e2e proves a chunk that shares no words with the learner's statement is retrieved when its embedding is nearest, and that the default (no capability) stays lexical.

evidence.note: Shared contract suite (memory + Postgres in CI) gained the vector-retrieval test: a query embedding ranks the semantically nearest chunk over chunks the query shares no words with, bounded by owner and gap exactly like lexical retrieval; setChunkEmbeddings is owner-scoped.

GAP-033.notes: scripts/compile-math-gap.ts is the sibling of smoke-compile.ts the task asked for. It exposes compileSeededMathGap(context, owner, key) - seed (idempotent, GAP-032) -> define -> compile -> assert all four acceptance criteria - used by both the script main and the deterministic test, so the script's assertions are exactly the test's. The compile key is fixed (gap-033-math-compile), making the script itself idempotent: a re-run deduplicates to the original run. Two pipeline facts surfaced while writing this: (1) a deduplicated repeat returns no curriculumId and a summary-only days list (audioSegments: 0), so the script resolves the run's curriculum via getForRun/getCurrentForGap and asserts Day 1 from repository artefacts rather than the outcome; (2) the per-process memory object store (GAP-026) cannot serve audio bytes on a cross-process re-run, so the FAKE-AUDIO: stub-byte check is strict on a fresh compile and explicitly reported (warn + audioStubBytesVerified=false) on a dedupe re-run - the pipeline verified audio integrity before publishing and the artefact rows (kind/mediaType/checksum) survive in Postgres. Plan validation uses the plan-validation.test.ts pattern: findPlanViolations on the stored plan with satisfiedExternalPrerequisites = referenceNormalisation().assumedPrerequisites + referenceDiagnostic().demonstratedCapabilities, exactly what compile.ts passes. No API/schema change (script + test only), so specs/ is untouched; no migration; no new runtime telemetry (the script drives the existing pipeline, which already emits full_course_publication_latency_ms and audit findings).

evidence.note: 13 tests. The live backend speaks OpenAI-compatible chat-completions over plain fetch (no SDK): bearer auth, response_format json_object, the contract named in the system prompt, evidence passed through inside the fence, temperature/max_tokens/timeout forwarded. Failures are typed LiveProviderErrors with a retryable flag (429/5xx/network retryable; 400/JSON/usage failures not). Usage is required because the wrapper cannot account for a call whose cost it cannot measure; cost is integer millicents rounded up from an env-overridable price table (defaults track deepseek-chat list prices).

14 tests. The live TTS wrapper computes the transcript-linked checksum (identical to the fake's, so memory/SQL/pipeline integrity checks hold for live runs), estimates duration with the same 14-characters-per-second heuristic the domain segmenter uses, forwards text/voice/locale verbatim, wraps engine failures in LiveSynthesisError naming the segment, and charges 0 by default (free endpoint) with an optional per-thousand-characters price. The Google Translate TTS engine is plain fetch with the gTTS query shape, chunks long segments at word boundaries under the endpoint cap, hard-splits overlong words, maps regional locales to language codes, and throws typed errors on HTTP and network failure.
